additional_concerns: Neither candidate has executable meaning. Retrieval success and the unsupported structural check establish no legal or executable correctness.

Paragraph 10 does not supply a complete supervision or outcome standard. Actual authority, supervisory conduct and outcomes require separate evidence; no arrangement facts are supplied. Missing evidence is not substantive failure, and an incident alone does not establish loss of accountability.

The allocation candidate leaves supervisory discharge unresolved. The performance candidate's authority, supervision and satisfactory-outcome formulation is an interpretive assessment framework, not an expressly enumerated statutory test.

Paragraph 14's request qualifier most directly attaches to demonstration. Footnote 5 supports a harmonised reading and a rival independent-demonstration reading; neither absence of a request nor confirmation establishes SFC satisfaction. The scope of the high-confidence phrase also requires care.

Paragraph 15 concerns requested third-party audit or verification of three specified subjects; paragraph 16 concerns a requested legal opinion supporting the application. Neither is an automatic condition of retained accountability.

The supplied Tokenised Securities Circular paragraph 13 corroborates responsibility despite outsourcing within its stated intermediary scope. It neither automatically applies to every Product Provider nor supplies the missing performance standard. It must not be confused with paragraph 13 of the product circular incorporated by footnote 5.
The complete paragraphs 10–13, footnote 2 and applicable Appendix factors are not supplied. Their contents cannot be inferred from references, and no external dependency identifiers are available.
